doc.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Working with Ben Pollack's Dixieland band
summary: He played nights with Pollack's six-piece band alongside radio work; Matty Matlock was in it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well as I say this was 19 — early 50s, maybe late 40s with the ‘49 or ‘50 or something. Anyhow so at that period I was doing a few radio shows and then I started to work — Ben Pollack called me. And I always thought, gee, that would be the ideal. You’d have a couple of radio shows, and then you work with a good jazz band in some club at night. And so that finally happened. And after a while I wasn’t too crazy about going to the same place every night and playing the same tunes. You know, even with good guys. So you live and learn. But it was a good career move though. I mean I started out to be a jazz piano player, so I couldn’t not do that if somebody asked me to do it. And I was with Pollack a long time. And I had probably two radio shows. I don’t think I was getting record dates at that time. Because that would have conflicted. Because record dates are in the evening a lot. Nowadays they send a sub and all that. I don’t think Pollack would have been too crazy about that. Although I probably could have done it. It never came up.
This was what, a five or six piece group?

Yeah. Like a Dixieland band, three horns and three rhythm. And Matty Matlock was in the band. He had record dates and stuff. And he used to send, like if they had a good sub that stood by — I probably could have done it. But anyhow it didn’t come up. The job finished. It seems like everything kind of coordinated just right. It finished and then I started to get record date calls. Funny, that was the days of, I guess I don’t know if they even called it rock & roll or rhythm & blues, with the triplets in the right hand [scats]. I started getting a lot of calls like that, where that’s what they wanted.
